            applied_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL

    CREATE TABLE documents (
        key TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (schema_version > 0),
        document_json TEXT NOT NULL,
        updated_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE TABLE quarantined_documents (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        source_key TEXT NOT NULL,
        schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
        document_json TEXT NOT NULL,
        reason_code TEXT NOT NULL,
        quarantined_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE TABLE agents (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
        engine_json TEXT NOT NULL,
        purpose TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(purpose) <= 4000),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE TABLE workspaces (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        display_name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(display_name) BETWEEN 1 AND 255),
        canonical_root TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
        last_opened_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX agents_created_at_idx
        ON agents(created_at_unix_ms, id);
    CREATE INDEX workspaces_recent_idx
        ON workspaces(last_opened_at_unix_ms DESC, id);
    CREATE TABLE chat_archive_metadata (

        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,

        ON chat_threads(updated_at_unix_ms DESC, id);

    ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN profile_schema_version INTEGER

    -- 524288 bytes matches MAX_AGENT_PROFILE_BYTES at the write boundary.
    ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN profile_json TEXT
        CHECK (
            profile_json IS NULL
            OR length(CAST(profile_json AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 2 AND 524288

    CREATE TRIGGER agents_cascade_chat_threads
    AFTER DELETE ON agents

    END;
    -- Filesystem-backed Agent homes cannot participate in the SQLite
    -- transaction that removes the profile, chats, and routines. Persist
    -- the cleanup intent in the same commit so an
    -- interrupted or failed recursive deletion is retried after restart.
    CREATE TABLE pending_agent_home_deletions (
        agent_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(agent_id) = 36
            AND substr(agent_id, 9, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(agent_id, 14, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(agent_id, 19, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(agent_id, 24, 1) = '-'
            AND length(replace(agent_id, '-', '')) = 32
            AND agent_id NOT GLOB '*[^0-9A-Fa-f-]*'
        ),
        requested_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (requested_at_unix_ms >= 0)
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE TRIGGER chat_threads_require_agent_insert
    BEFORE INSERT ON chat_threads
    WHEN NEW.profile_id IS NOT NULL
         AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM agents WHERE id = NEW.profile_id)
    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'owned chat profile missing');
    END;
    CREATE TRIGGER chat_threads_require_agent_update
    BEFORE UPDATE OF profile_id ON chat_threads
    WHEN NEW.profile_id IS NOT NULL
         AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM agents WHERE id = NEW.profile_id)
    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'owned chat profile missing');
    END;
    -- Each routine is an independently bounded, versioned JSON document.
    -- Relational projections make due scans and ownership checks possible
    -- without trusting or partially decoding the payload.
    CREATE TABLE agent_routines (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(id) = 36
            AND substr(id, 9, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(id, 14, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(id, 19, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(id, 24, 1) = '-'
            AND length(replace(id, '-', '')) = 32
            AND id NOT GLOB '*[^0-9A-Fa-f-]*'
        ),
        agent_id TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(agent_id) = 36
            AND substr(agent_id, 9, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(agent_id, 14, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(agent_id, 19, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(agent_id, 24, 1) = '-'
            AND length(replace(agent_id, '-', '')) = 32
            AND agent_id NOT GLOB '*[^0-9A-Fa-f-]*'
        ),
        schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (schema_version > 0),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        next_run_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (
            next_run_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms
        ),
        enabled INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (enabled IN (0, 1)),
        -- 655360 bytes matches MAX_ROUTINE_PAYLOAD_BYTES.
        payload BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (
            typeof(payload) = 'blob'
            AND length(payload) BETWEEN 2 AND 655360
        )
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX agent_routines_agent_created_idx
        ON agent_routines(agent_id, created_at_unix_ms, id);
    CREATE INDEX agent_routines_due_idx
        ON agent_routines(next_run_at_unix_ms, agent_id, id)
        WHERE enabled = 1;
    CREATE TRIGGER agent_routines_require_agent_insert
    BEFORE INSERT ON agent_routines
    WHEN NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM agents WHERE id = NEW.agent_id)
    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'routine agent missing');
    END;
    CREATE TRIGGER agent_routines_require_agent_update
    BEFORE UPDATE ON agent_routines
    WHEN NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM agents WHERE id = NEW.agent_id)
    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'routine agent missing');
    END;
    CREATE TRIGGER agents_cascade_routines
    AFTER DELETE ON agents
    BEGIN
        DELETE FROM agent_routines WHERE agent_id = OLD.id;
    END;
    -- A future chat-runtime migration will persist a unique
    -- (routine_id, scheduled_for_unix_ms) occurrence key beside its fresh
    -- thread. Keeping that replay metadata out of routine definitions avoids
    -- pretending this migration provides exactly-once provider execution.
    -- Notification history and builder notification preferences are versioned
    -- JSON documents in the existing documents table:
    --   notification-archive (schema 3)
    --   notification-preferences (schema 1)
    -- No relational tables: the ledger is a bounded 100-row inbox, not a query
    -- surface. This migration exists so schema_migrations records the slice.
    SELECT 1;
        
    -- UUID identity checks deliberately remain case-insensitive so a planted
    -- uppercase alias cannot bypass compare-and-swap identity. Match that
    -- lookup with an index while retaining duplicate detection in Rust.
    CREATE INDEX chat_threads_id_nocase_idx
        ON chat_threads(id COLLATE NOCASE);
    -- Backend-owned idempotency receipts bridge the Routine definition and
    -- its fresh Chat insert. Request identifiers are opaque replay keys, not
    -- renderer authority: application code still verifies exact ownership,
    -- the observed Routine revision, and the chat-capable Agent profile.
    CREATE TABLE routine_run_receipts (
        request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(request_id) = 36
            AND substr(request_id, 9, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(request_id, 14, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(request_id, 19, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(request_id, 24, 1) = '-'
            AND length(replace(request_id, '-', '')) = 32
            AND request_id NOT GLOB '*[^0-9A-Fa-f-]*'
        ),
        agent_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        routine_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        scheduled_for_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (scheduled_for_unix_ms >= 0),
        thread_id TEXT,
        state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            state IN ('claimed', 'started', 'completed', 'failed')
        ),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        settled_at_unix_ms INTEGER CHECK (
            settled_at_unix_ms IS NULL OR settled_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms
        ),
        CHECK (
            state = 'failed'
            OR thread_id IS NOT NULL
        ),
        UNIQUE(routine_id, scheduled_for_unix_ms),
        UNIQUE(thread_id)
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX routine_run_receipts_agent_state_idx
        ON routine_run_receipts(agent_id, state, created_at_unix_ms, request_id);
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX routine_run_receipts_one_active_agent_idx
        ON routine_run_receipts(agent_id)
        WHERE state IN ('claimed', 'started');
    CREATE TRIGGER agents_cascade_routine_run_receipts
    AFTER DELETE ON agents
    BEGIN
        DELETE FROM routine_run_receipts WHERE agent_id = OLD.id;
    END;
    -- First-party Agent tool mutations span SQLite authority and Agent-home
    -- files. A bounded receipt records the exact identity/input digest and
    -- planned filesystem revisions before the CAS write. Replays can then
    -- prove whether the write is pending, already durable, or conflicted.
    CREATE TABLE agent_tool_receipts (
        idempotency_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(idempotency_key) = 36
            AND substr(idempotency_key, 9, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(idempotency_key, 14, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(idempotency_key, 19, 1) = '-'
            AND substr(idempotency_key, 24, 1) = '-'
            AND length(replace(idempotency_key, '-', '')) = 32
            AND idempotency_key NOT GLOB '*[^0-9A-Fa-f-]*'
        ),
        profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        thread_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        tool_name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            tool_name IN (
                'memory_add', 'memory_update', 'memory_forget', 'skill_used'
            )
        ),
        input_digest TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(input_digest) = 64
            AND input_digest NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'
        ),
        state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('pending', 'succeeded', 'failed')),
        target_kind TEXT CHECK (target_kind IN ('memory', 'user', 'skill')),
        target_id TEXT CHECK (
            target_id IS NULL
            OR length(CAST(target_id AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 1 AND 256
        ),
        pre_revision TEXT CHECK (
            pre_revision IS NULL
            OR (length(pre_revision) = 64 AND pre_revision NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*')
        ),
        post_revision TEXT CHECK (
            post_revision IS NULL
            OR (length(post_revision) = 64 AND post_revision NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*')
        ),
        -- Only non-sensitive deterministic metadata (currently the native
        -- skill-use timestamp) belongs here; memory content is never copied
        -- into SQLite.
        plan_marker TEXT CHECK (
            plan_marker IS NULL
            OR length(CAST(plan_marker AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 1 AND 256
        ),
        result_json TEXT CHECK (
            result_json IS NULL
            OR length(CAST(result_json AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 2 AND 24000
        ),
        error_code TEXT CHECK (
            error_code IS NULL
            OR length(CAST(error_code AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 1 AND 64
        ),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        settled_at_unix_ms INTEGER CHECK (
            settled_at_unix_ms IS NULL OR settled_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms
        ),
        CHECK (
            (state = 'pending' AND result_json IS NULL AND error_code IS NULL
                AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NULL)
            OR (state = 'succeeded' AND result_json IS NOT NULL
                AND error_code IS NULL AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
            OR (state = 'failed' AND result_json IS NULL
                AND error_code IS NOT NULL AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
        )
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX agent_tool_receipts_profile_state_idx
        ON agent_tool_receipts(profile_id, state, created_at_unix_ms, idempotency_key);
    CREATE TRIGGER agents_cascade_agent_tool_receipts
    AFTER DELETE ON agents
    BEGIN
        DELETE FROM agent_tool_receipts WHERE profile_id = OLD.id;
    END;
    -- Agent mail is one bounded, strictly validated snapshot. The revision is
    -- the application-layer CAS token; SQLite never interprets message text.
    CREATE TABLE agent_message_ledger (
        singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL CHECK (singleton = 1),
        revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (revision > 0),
        snapshot BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (
            typeof(snapshot) = 'blob'
            AND length(snapshot) BETWEEN 2 AND 1048576
        ),
        updated_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (updated_at_unix_ms >= 0)
    ) STRICT;
    -- The model supplies an idempotency key, never a message delivery key.
    -- This receipt binds that request to the native-minted delivery/message
    -- identities and exact sender thread before the tool can report success.
    CREATE TABLE agent_message_send_receipts (
        idempotency_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        sender_profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        sender_thread_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        recipient_profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        input_digest TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(input_digest) = 64
            AND input_digest NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'
        ),
        delivery_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        message_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        disposition TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            disposition IN ('wake_requested', 'queued')
        ),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0)
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX agent_message_receipts_sender_idx
        ON agent_message_send_receipts(
            sender_profile_id, sender_thread_id, created_at_unix_ms, idempotency_key
        );
    -- Idle-recipient sends commit an app-owned outbox intent in the same
    -- transaction as the mail snapshot. No provider process or renderer owns
    -- this state, and a replay cannot create a second wake for one message.
    CREATE TABLE agent_message_wake_intents (
        message_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        recipient_profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        CHECK (message_id <> recipient_profile_id)
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX agent_message_wake_recipient_idx
        ON agent_message_wake_intents(recipient_profile_id, created_at_unix_ms, message_id);
    CREATE TRIGGER agents_cascade_agent_message_wakes
    AFTER DELETE ON agents
    BEGIN
        DELETE FROM agent_message_wake_intents WHERE recipient_profile_id = OLD.id;
    END;
    CREATE TRIGGER agents_cascade_agent_message_receipts
    AFTER DELETE ON agents
    BEGIN
        DELETE FROM agent_message_send_receipts
        WHERE sender_profile_id = OLD.id OR recipient_profile_id = OLD.id;
    END;
    -- One receipt admits at most one reflection provider attempt for one
    -- exact persisted direct-Agent transcript revision. Transcript/prompt
    -- text never enters this table.
    CREATE TABLE agent_reflection_receipts (
        profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        thread_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        transcript_revision TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(transcript_revision) = 64
            AND transcript_revision NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'
        ),
        state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            state IN ('pending', 'succeeded', 'blocked', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'stale')
        ),
        error_code TEXT CHECK (
            error_code IN (
                'provider_tool_transport_unavailable',
                'provider_failed',
                'cancelled',
                'stale_authority'
            )
        ),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        settled_at_unix_ms INTEGER CHECK (
            settled_at_unix_ms IS NULL OR settled_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms
        ),
        PRIMARY KEY (profile_id, thread_id, transcript_revision),
        CHECK (
            (state = 'pending' AND error_code IS NULL AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NULL)
            OR (state = 'succeeded' AND error_code IS NULL AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
            OR (state = 'blocked'
                AND error_code = 'provider_tool_transport_unavailable'
                AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
            OR (state = 'failed' AND error_code = 'provider_failed'
                AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
            OR (state = 'cancelled' AND error_code = 'cancelled'
                AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
            OR (state = 'stale' AND error_code = 'stale_authority'
                AND settled_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
        )
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX agent_reflection_receipts_state_idx
        ON agent_reflection_receipts(state, created_at_unix_ms, profile_id, thread_id);
    CREATE TRIGGER agents_cascade_agent_reflection_receipts
    AFTER DELETE ON agents
    BEGIN
        DELETE FROM agent_reflection_receipts WHERE profile_id = OLD.id;
    END;
    -- A receipt is committed in the same IMMEDIATE transaction as every
    -- accepted legacy row. The source fingerprint is content-derived, so a
    -- restart or replay cannot duplicate an import.
    CREATE TABLE legacy_import_receipts (
        fingerprint TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(fingerprint) = 64
            AND fingerprint NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'
        ),
        report_version INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (report_version > 0),
        report_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(CAST(report_json AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 2 AND 1048576
        ),
        applied_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (applied_at_unix_ms >= 0)
    ) STRICT;
    -- Legacy macOS paths are inert labels. They are deliberately separate
    -- from workspaces.canonical_root and can acquire authority only through a
    -- later native folder picker enrollment.
    CREATE TABLE legacy_import_place_labels (
        import_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        receipt_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
        display_name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(display_name) BETWEEN 1 AND 1024),
        requires_reenrollment INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (requires_reenrollment = 1),
        FOREIGN KEY(receipt_fingerprint)
            REFERENCES legacy_import_receipts(fingerprint) ON DELETE CASCADE
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX legacy_import_place_receipt_idx
        ON legacy_import_place_labels(receipt_fingerprint, import_id);
    -- The legacy transcript is intentionally not represented. This table
    -- keeps only bounded, non-executable thread metadata and never stores
    -- item bodies, attachments, tool payloads, errors, cursors, or cwd data.
    CREATE TABLE legacy_import_chat_metadata (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        receipt_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
        profile_id TEXT,
        routine_id TEXT,
        title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(CAST(title AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 1 AND 4096),
        provider TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(provider) BETWEEN 1 AND 32),
        mode TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('accept_edits', 'full_access', 'read_only')),
        source_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            source_status IN ('idle', 'running', 'waiting', 'error')
        ),
        planned INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (planned IN (0, 1)),
        source_item_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (
            source_item_count BETWEEN 0 AND 10000
        ),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        updated_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (
            updated_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms
        ),
        FOREIGN KEY(receipt_fingerprint)
            REFERENCES legacy_import_receipts(fingerprint) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        FOREIGN KEY(profile_id) REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        FOREIGN KEY(routine_id) REFERENCES agent_routines(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX legacy_import_chat_recent_idx
        ON legacy_import_chat_metadata(updated_at_unix_ms DESC, id);
    CREATE INDEX legacy_import_chat_receipt_idx
        ON legacy_import_chat_metadata(receipt_fingerprint, id);
    -- A wake claim binds one exact recipient to one backend-minted fresh
    -- Chat before provider preflight. Message text and sender identity remain
    -- in the bounded mail ledger; this table contains only opaque authority.
    CREATE TABLE agent_message_wake_runs (
        claim_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        owner_instance_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        recipient_profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        thread_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('claimed', 'launching', 'started', 'ambiguous')),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        lease_expires_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (lease_expires_at_unix_ms > created_at_unix_ms),
        handoff_started_at_unix_ms INTEGER CHECK (handoff_started_at_unix_ms IS NULL OR handoff_started_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms),
        started_at_unix_ms INTEGER CHECK (started_at_unix_ms IS NULL OR started_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms),
        CHECK (
            (state = 'claimed' AND handoff_started_at_unix_ms IS NULL AND started_at_unix_ms IS NULL)
            OR (state IN ('launching', 'ambiguous') AND handoff_started_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL AND started_at_unix_ms IS NULL)
            OR (state = 'started' AND handoff_started_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL AND started_at_unix_ms IS NOT NULL)
        ),
        FOREIGN KEY(recipient_profile_id) REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE TABLE agent_message_wake_run_items (
        claim_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        message_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        ordinal INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (ordinal BETWEEN 0 AND 4),
        FOREIGN KEY(claim_id) REFERENCES agent_message_wake_runs(claim_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX agent_message_wake_run_item_order_idx
        ON agent_message_wake_run_items(claim_id, ordinal);
    CREATE INDEX agent_message_wake_run_state_idx
        ON agent_message_wake_runs(state, created_at_unix_ms, claim_id);
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX agent_message_wake_active_recipient_idx
        ON agent_message_wake_runs(recipient_profile_id)
        WHERE state IN ('claimed', 'launching', 'started');
    -- History rails need only a bounded projection, never the transcript
    -- payload. The projection is rebuilt once by trusted Rust after this
    -- migration, then maintained transactionally by the triggers below.
    CREATE TABLE chat_thread_summaries (
        thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        profile_id TEXT,
        place_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (place_count BETWEEN 0 AND 64),
        routine_id TEXT,
        title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(CAST(title AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 1 AND 4096
        ),
        provider TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (provider IN ('claude-code', 'codex')),
        status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('idle', 'running', 'waiting', 'error')),
        has_content INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (has_content IN (0, 1)),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        updated_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (
            updated_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms
        ),
        FOREIGN KEY(thread_id) REFERENCES chat_threads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    ) STRICT;
    CREATE INDEX chat_thread_summaries_recent_idx
        ON chat_thread_summaries(updated_at_unix_ms DESC, thread_id);
    CREATE INDEX chat_thread_summaries_profile_recent_idx
        ON chat_thread_summaries(profile_id, updated_at_unix_ms DESC, thread_id);
    -- Archive quota checks are on every streaming checkpoint. Keeping the
    -- aggregate in the same transaction turns an O(thread-count) SUM into a
    -- constant-time read without weakening the existing byte ceiling.
    CREATE TABLE chat_archive_totals (
        singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL CHECK (singleton = 1),
        thread_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (thread_count >= 0),
        payload_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (payload_bytes >= 0)
    ) STRICT;
    INSERT INTO chat_archive_totals(singleton, thread_count, payload_bytes)
    SELECT 1, count(*), COALESCE(sum(length(payload)), 0)
    FROM chat_threads;
    INSERT INTO chat_archive_metadata(key, value)
    VALUES ('summary_projection_version', '0');
    CREATE TRIGGER chat_threads_summary_after_insert
    AFTER INSERT ON chat_threads
    BEGIN
        INSERT OR IGNORE INTO chat_thread_summaries(
            thread_id, profile_id, place_count, routine_id, title, provider,
            status, has_content, created_at_unix_ms, updated_at_unix_ms
        ) SELECT
            NEW.id,
            NEW.profile_id,
            json_array_length(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT), '$.places'),
            json_extract(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT), '$.routineId'),
            json_extract(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT), '$.title'),
            json_extract(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT), '$.provider'),
            json_extract(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT), '$.status'),
            CASE
                WHEN json_array_length(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT), '$.items') > 0
                THEN 1 ELSE 0
            END,
            json_extract(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT), '$.createdAtUnixMs'),
            NEW.updated_at_unix_ms
        WHERE json_valid(CAST(NEW.payload AS TEXT));
        UPDATE chat_archive_totals
        SET thread_count = thread_count + 1,
            payload_bytes = payload_bytes + length(NEW.payload)
        WHERE singleton = 1;
    END;
    CREATE TRIGGER chat_threads_summary_after_update
    AFTER UPDATE OF profile_id, updated_at_unix_ms, payload ON chat_threads
    BEGIN
        DELETE FROM chat_thread_summaries WHERE thread_id = OLD.id;

            status, has_content, created_at_unix_ms, updated_at_unix_ms

        UPDATE chat_archive_totals
        SET payload_bytes = payload_bytes - length(OLD.payload) + length(NEW.payload)
        WHERE singleton = 1;
    END;

    -- Chat mode becomes T3 Code-style threads: a general chat can bind to one
    -- enrolled workspace (`$.workspaceId`, an opaque id ??? never a path) and be
    -- pinned above the workspace bands (`$.pinned`). The three ACP harnesses
    -- (Cursor, Grok, OpenCode) now run Chat turns too, so the provider check
    -- widens. SQLite cannot alter a CHECK in place, so the projection table is
    -- rebuilt and every existing row is carried over with the new columns
    -- backfilled from the thread payload.
    DROP TRIGGER chat_threads_summary_after_insert;
    DROP TRIGGER chat_threads_summary_after_update;
    DROP TRIGGER chat_threads_summary_after_delete;
    CREATE TABLE chat_thread_summaries_v16 (
        thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        profile_id TEXT,
        place_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (place_count BETWEEN 0 AND 64),
        routine_id TEXT,
        title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            length(CAST(title AS BLOB)) BETWEEN 1 AND 4096
        ),
        provider TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
            provider IN ('claude-code', 'codex', 'cursor', 'grok', 'open-code')
        ),
        status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('idle', 'running', 'waiting', 'error')),
        has_content INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (has_content IN (0, 1)),
        tab_order REAL,
        workspace_id TEXT NULL,
        pinned INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (pinned IN (0, 1)),
        created_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (created_at_unix_ms >= 0),
        updated_at_unix_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (
            updated_at_unix_ms >= created_at_unix_ms
        ),
        FOREIGN KEY(thread_id) REFERENCES chat_threads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    ) STRICT;
    INSERT INTO chat_thread_summaries_v16(
        thread_id, profile_id, place_count, routine_id, title, provider,
        status, has_content, tab_order, workspace_id, pinned,
        created_at_unix_ms, updated_at_unix_ms
    ) SELECT
        s.thread_id, s.profile_id, s.place_count, s.routine_id, s.title, s.provider,
        s.status, s.has_content, s.tab_order,
        json_extract(CAST(t.payload AS TEXT), '$.workspaceId'),
        CASE
            WHEN json_extract(CAST(t.payload AS TEXT), '$.pinned') = 1 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END,
        s.created_at_unix_ms, s.updated_at_unix_ms
    FROM chat_thread_summaries AS s
    JOIN chat_threads AS t ON t.id = s.thread_id
    WHERE json_valid(CAST(t.payload AS TEXT));

>>>keep-a-memoryKeep a memoryWhat's worth remembering between chats.---
name: keep-a-memory
description: Decide what to write into MEMORY.md and USER.md and what to leave out. Use at the end of any task where you learned something durable about the builder, their business, their accounts, their standards or their tools ??? and any time you notice you had to re-derive something you should already have known.
# Keep a memory
Your memory is the only thing that crosses from this chat into the next one.
It is also loaded into every turn, so every entry you add costs context
forever. Both facts point the same way: write few entries, and make each one
worth its rent.
There are two files. Use the memory tools with `target`:
- **`target=memory`** (default) ??? your notes. Conventions, decisions and why,
  environment, tool quirks, mistakes not to repeat.
- **`target=user`** ??? who the builder is. Preferences, names, how they like
  work delivered, constraints that belong to them rather than to the job.
Each entry can be a few lines. Entries are separated by the `??` mark; do not
put that mark inside an entry.
## What earns an entry
- **Stable facts.** Names, handles, who owns which account, folder and repo
  paths, tool choices, who decides what.
- **Preferences with a shape.** "Wants the number before the explanation."
  "Signs off as the team, never as an individual." Not "likes good writing."
- **Decisions and their reason.** The reason is the part that stops a decision
  being relitigated every quarter. "Postgres over SQLite ??? needs concurrent
  writers."
- **Constraints.** Recurring deadlines, budgets, things that must never happen.
- **Corrections.** You were told you got something wrong. Record the corrected
  version, not the story of the mistake.
## What does not
- **What you did.** The chat already holds it. "Wrote the launch post" is not
  memory.
- **Anything one command retrieves.** The file tree, a package version, today's
  date.
- **Secrets.** Keys, tokens, passwords, private customer data. If a credential
  is missing, name which one and let the builder supply it.
- **Guesses.** An entry in memory reads as established fact to every future
  turn. If you are not sure, leave it out or prefix it `unconfirmed:`.
- **Anything already in your brief.** The brief is loaded too; repeating it
  spends context twice.
## How to write it
One entry, one fact, present tense, no preamble. A label helps:
    Brand voice: "builders", never "users". Ships copy without em dashes.
    Launch posts go out through the X plugin, never by hand.
    Staging DB resets nightly ??? never leave fixtures there.
Use `memory_add`. Do not append with a shell redirect. Do not rewrite the
whole file to slot something into the middle ??? add, or replace the one entry
that changed.
## The cap is a hard stop
MEMORY.md and USER.md have character caps. A write that would pass one is
refused and lists the current entries. That is not a failure to retry blindly:
in the same turn, `memory_update` overlapping entries into shorter ones or
`memory_forget` stale ones, then retry the add. Never tail-trim. Never drop
an old fact just because a new one arrived.
## Maintenance is part of the job
- **A contradiction is a bug.** When something you learn makes an existing
  entry false, update that entry. Never add the new fact underneath and leave
  both standing.
- **Prune on sight.** If you read an entry that has stopped being true, forget
  it in the same turn you noticed.
- **Length means you were too specific.** Collapse five entries about five
  individual posts into one about how posts work here.
## The test
Before you write an entry, ask: *if a version of me with no memory of this
conversation read only this entry, would it act differently ??? and correctly?*
If no, do not write it.
write-a-skillWrite a skillTurn a procedure it just worked out into a reusable one.---
name: write-a-skill
description: Turn a procedure you just worked out into a reusable SKILL.md in your own skills folder. Use when you finish something non-obvious you will plausibly be asked for again, when you notice you are repeating the same sequence across chats, or when a skill you followed turned out to be wrong and needs correcting.
# Write a skill
Memory is what you know. A skill is what you can *do* ??? the steps, in order,
with the traps marked. Write one when the second attempt should be faster than
the first was.
## When to write one
Two of these three is enough:
1. You will plausibly be asked for this again.
2. Getting it right took work ??? an order that matters, a flag that isn't
   obvious, a failure you hit and had to recover from.
3. You could not have reconstructed it from the task description alone.
**Do not** write a skill for something a single prompt already handles well, and
do not write one to record how one task turned out ??? that is memory, or it is
nothing.
## Shape
`<your skills folder>/<kebab-case-name>/SKILL.md`
    ---
    name: kebab-case-name
    description: What it does, then WHEN TO USE IT. The "when" is what fires it ??? write the words a future task would actually contain.
    ---
    # Title
    One line on what this is for.
    ## Steps
    1. ???
    ## Traps
    - ???
The `description` is the only part always in context; everything else is read
after it fires. So the description does the entire job of retrieval ??? spend your
care there. Name the *situation*, not the capability: "when a release is cut and
the changelog needs writing" beats "changelog expertise".
## Writing the body
- **Imperative and specific.** "Run `x`, then check `y`" beats "consider
  checking".
- **Exact strings.** Real commands, real paths, real field names. A skill that
  says "the config file" sends the next run looking all over again.
- **Mark the traps.** The thing that bit you is the highest-value line in the
  file. Say what goes wrong and what to do instead.
- **Short.** Past a screen or two it is either two skills or a document that
  belongs in the workspace.
- **No narrative.** Nobody needs to know how you discovered this.
## Editing beats adding
Before writing a new skill, read the descriptions of the ones you already have.
If one covers this situation and is merely thin or wrong, fix it. Two skills that
each half-fire on the same task is worse than one that fires cleanly.
When a skill you followed misled you: correct the file in the same turn, and say
in your reply that you did ??? the builder should know your instructions changed.
research-a-questionResearch a questionAnswer from current sources, not from memory.---
name: research-a-question
description: Answer a factual question with current, sourced information rather than from memory. Use when asked to look something up, compare vendors or options, check what a competitor is doing, verify a claim, find current pricing, limits or API behaviour ??? and any time you catch yourself about to answer confidently about something that changes.
# Research a question
The failure mode is not being unable to find the answer. It is answering from
training data in a confident voice about something that moved last month.
## Before you look
**Separate the question from the ask.** "Is Stripe cheaper than Adyen" is a
question; "should we switch" is a decision that needs the question answered
first. Say which one you are doing.
**Decide what would settle it.** Name the source type that counts before you
start: vendor pricing page, official docs, filing, changelog, benchmark. If you
cannot name one, the question is an opinion and should be answered as one.
## Looking
1. **Primary sources first.** The vendor's own docs and pricing page, the
   project's repo and release notes, the regulator's filing. A blog post about a
   pricing page is a copy of a page that may since have changed.
2. **Date everything.** Find when the source was published or last updated. An
   undated page is weak evidence about anything that changes.
3. **Two sources for anything load-bearing.** One source is a claim; two that
   agree and were written independently is a fact. Two that agree because one
   copied the other is still one source.
4. **Look for the contradiction on purpose.** Search for the counter-case, the
   deprecation notice, the "why we moved off X". Confirming evidence arrives on
   its own; disconfirming evidence has to be sought.
5. **Stop when the next source stops changing the answer.** Not when you run out
   of results.
## Reporting
Lead with the answer. Then the evidence, then what is still open.
> **Answer:** ???
> **As of:** the date of the freshest source you used
> **Sources:** title ??? url ??? date, one per line
> **Confidence:** what you verified directly vs. inferred
> **Open:** what you could not confirm, and what would confirm it
Rules for the write-up:
- **Mark inference as inference.** "The docs don't say; the changelog implies"
  is honest and useful. Presenting it as fact is neither.
- **Quote numbers exactly, with their units and currency.** Do not round a price
  or convert a currency silently.
- **If you could not find it, say so plainly and stop.** "I could not find a
  published limit; the docs cover X and Y but not this" is a complete answer.
  Constructing a plausible number is the single worst outcome available.
- **Never cite a URL you did not open.**
## Then remember it
A researched answer with a shelf life belongs in memory with its date, so the
next turn knows both the answer and when it will need rechecking.
draft-for-a-readerDraft for a readerWrite for one person and one action, then cut.---
name: draft-for-a-reader
description: Write or revise anything a person will read ??? a post, an email, release notes, docs, landing-page copy, an announcement, a summary. Use whenever the deliverable is prose rather than something that runs, and whenever you are asked to tighten, shorten, punch up, or rewrite existing copy.
# Draft for a reader
A draft is not finished when it says everything true. It is finished when one
specific person can read it once and act.
**A project's own voice outranks this file.** If the workspace, your brief, or
your memory carries brand or style rules, follow those and use this only for what
they leave open.
## Before the first sentence
Answer three things, in writing if the piece is long:
1. **Who reads this,** and what they already know. A changelog for existing users
   and a launch post for strangers share no sentences.
2. **What they should do or believe** afterwards. One thing. If you cannot name
   it, you are not ready to draft.
3. **Where they meet it** ??? inbox, timeline, docs page, terminal. That sets the
   length before you write a word.
## Drafting
- **Lead with the outcome.** The first sentence carries the news. Background is
  for readers who want it, and it goes after.
- **One idea per paragraph.** If a paragraph needs "also", it is two.
- **Specifics instead of adjectives.** "Cuts the build from 90s to 12s" does the
  work "dramatically faster" only claims.
- **Verbs over nouns.** "We shipped X" beats "the shipping of X was completed".
- **Say the number, the name, the date.** Vagueness reads as either ignorance or
  spin.
- **Write the ending on purpose.** Ask for the one action, or stop. Never trail
  off into a summary of what the reader just read.
## Then cut
Revision is where the piece gets good. Do a pass for each:
- **Cut the throat-clearing.** "In today's fast-moving landscape", "It's worth
  noting that", "I hope this finds you well". Delete the first sentence and see
  if anything was lost.
- **Cut hedges.** "Somewhat", "arguably", "we believe", "may potentially". Either
  you claim it or you don't.
- **Cut the restatement.** A conclusion that repeats the intro means one of them
  is dead weight.
- **Kill filler intensifiers.** "Very", "really", "truly", "incredibly".
- **Read it aloud.** Anything you stumble over, a reader stumbles over.
Target: 20???30% shorter than the first draft, saying the same things.
## Tells to avoid
These read as machine-written and cost the piece its credibility:
- Tricolon everywhere ??? "faster, cleaner, and more reliable" in every paragraph.
- "It's not just X, it's Y."
- Opening on a dictionary definition or a rhetorical question.
- Headers on a 200-word note.
- Bullets for prose that should be sentences, or sentences for data that should
  be a table.
- Emoji the reader did not ask for.
- Praising the thing instead of describing it.
## Handing it over
Deliver the draft, then one line on what you chose and what you were unsure of ???
the length, the audience you assumed, the claim you softened because you could
not verify it. That is the part the builder can actually act on.
root-causeRoot causeNarrow a problem to its cause before proposing a fix.---
name: root-cause
description: Narrow a problem to its actual cause before proposing a fix. Use when something fails intermittently, when the obvious fix did not work, when a metric moved and nobody knows why, when an automation silently stopped, or when the user asks "why is this happening". Stops the guess-and-check loop.
# Root cause
The symptom is where you noticed. The cause is where it went wrong. They are
rarely the same place ??? in a program, in a pipeline, in a campaign, or in a
process.
## Narrow before you fix
1. **State the symptom precisely.** "Upload fails" is not a symptom. "Uploads
   over 5MB return 200 but the stored object is 0 bytes, on staging only" is.
   "Signups dropped" is not; "signups from paid search fell 60% starting the 4th,
   organic flat" is.
2. **Find the boundary.** What is the smallest input that fails and the largest
   that works? Which environment, which account, which region, which day?
3. **Bisect something.** Version history, the input, the pipeline stage, the
   recipient list, the date range. Halve the search space each step.
4. **Prove the cause.** You have it when you can make the problem appear and
   disappear on demand by toggling one thing.
5. **Only then fix.**
## Signals worth trusting
- **The first frame you own is the interesting one.** A stack trace's top frame
  is where it threw, not where it broke; read down to your own code and look at
  what it was handed. The same goes for a report: the number that changed first
  matters more than the number someone noticed.
- **Intermittent means shared state.** Time, ordering, caching, a connection
  pool, a retry, a rate limit, a test that leaks. Nothing pure flakes.
- **"It works for me" is data.** The difference between the two cases *is* the
  bug ??? a version, an env var, a permission, a timezone, a locale, a plan tier.
- **Recent-change bias is usually right.** Check what shipped or changed just
  before the first report before theorising about anything older. Ask what
  changed that nobody thinks of as a change: a dependency, a vendor's default, a
  rotated key, a full disk.
## Anti-patterns
- Adding a guard where it broke. That hides whoever produced the bad value.
- Widening a `catch` until the error stops printing.
- Bumping a timeout on a race.
- Retrying something that is failing deterministically.
- Changing several things and re-running. Now you cannot attribute the result.
Each of these converts a reproducible problem into an unreproducible one.
## Report it like this
> **Symptom:** ???
> **Cause:** ??? (the exact place, and *why* it is wrong)
> **Evidence:** what you toggled to prove it
> **Fix:** ???
> **Left alone:** any related smell you deliberately did not touch
If you cannot fill in Evidence, you have a hypothesis rather than a cause ??? say
so in those words.

Use your tools when they make the work better, stay inside the ask, and say plainly when a tool is refused.  * BridgeMind One ??? browser Design Mode, page-world half.
 * Framework dev builds hang component identity off DOM nodes as JavaScript
 * expandos (React fibers, Vue instances, Svelte metadata). Those exist only
 * in the page's own world, so this helper must run there; the Design Mode
 * script (which may run in an isolated world) marks the node with
 * `data-bmone-probe`, dispatches `bmone-design-probe` on the document, and
 * reads the JSON this writes to `data-bmone-hints` synchronously.
 * It only reads expandos and writes one attribute on the probed node; the
 * page can call it too, which gains the page nothing it lacks already.
 * Static like its sibling: the host never interpolates into this source.
(function () {
  'use strict';
  if (window.__bmoneDesignHints === 1) return;
  window.__bmoneDesignHints = 1;
  var FRAMEWORK_INTERNALS = /^(InnerLayoutRouter|OuterLayoutRouter|LayoutRouter|RedirectErrorBoundary|RedirectBoundary|ErrorBoundary|ErrorBoundaryHandler|LoadingBoundary|HTTPAccessFallbackBoundary|HTTPAccessFallbackErrorBoundary|NotFoundBoundary|NotFoundErrorBoundary|RenderFromTemplateContext|ScrollAndFocusHandler|InnerScrollAndFocusHandler|ClientPageRoot|ClientSegmentRoot|AppRouter|Router|HotReload|ServerRoot|Root|MetadataBoundary|ViewportBoundary|OutletBoundary|SegmentViewNode|AppDevOverlayErrorBoundary|ReactDevOverlay|DevRootHTTPAccessFallbackBoundary)$/;
  var WRAPPERS = /^(Anonymous|Fragment|Suspense|StrictMode|Provider|Consumer|Context|ForwardRef|Memo|Lazy|Profiler)$/i;
  function reactNames(n) {
    var keys = Object.keys(n), key = null;
    for (var i = 0; i < keys.length; i++) {
      if (keys[i].indexOf('__reactFiber$') === 0 || keys[i].indexOf('__reactInternalInstance$') === 0) { key = keys[i]; break; }
    }
    if (!key) return null;
    var names = [], f = n[key], guard = 0;
    while (f && names.length < 4 && guard++ < 400) {
      var t = f.type;
      if (t && typeof t !== 'string') {
        var name = t.displayName || t.name ||
          (t.render && (t.render.displayName || t.render.name)) ||
          (t.type && (t.type.displayName || t.type.name)) || '';
        if (typeof name === 'string' && name && !WRAPPERS.test(name) && !FRAMEWORK_INTERNALS.test(name) &&
            name.charAt(0) !== '_' && names.indexOf(name) === -1) names.push(name);
      }
      f = f['return'];
    }
    return names.length ? names : null;
  function vueHint(n) {
    var c = n.__vueParentComponent, names = [], file = '';
    for (var i = 0; c && i < 4; i++, c = c.parent) {
      var t = c.type || {};
      var name = t.__name || t.name || '';
      if (!file && typeof t.__file === 'string') file = t.__file;
      if (typeof name === 'string' && name && names.indexOf(name) === -1) names.push(name);
    }
    return names.length || file ? { names: names, file: file } : null;
  function svelteSource(n) {
    for (var cur = n, i = 0; cur && i < 6; cur = cur.parentElement, i++) {
      var meta = cur.__svelte_meta;
      if (meta && meta.loc && typeof meta.loc.file === 'string') {
        return meta.loc.file + (typeof meta.loc.line === 'number' ? ':' + (meta.loc.line + 1) : '');

    return '';
  document.addEventListener('bmone-design-probe', function () {
    var n = document.querySelector('[data-bmone-probe]');
    if (!n) return;
    var answer = { components: null, source: '' };
    try {
      answer.components = reactNames(n);
      var vue = vueHint(n);
      if (vue) {
        if (!answer.components && vue.names.length) answer.components = vue.names;
        answer.source = vue.file;
      }
      if (!answer.source) answer.source = svelteSource(n);

// Copyright 2019-2024 Tauri Programme within The Commons Conservancy
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
;(function () {
  //-----------------------//
  // drag on mousedown and maximize on double click on Windows and Linux
  // while macOS maximization should be on mouseup and if the mouse
  // moves after the double click, it should be cancelled (see https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/8306)
  //-----------------------//
  const TAURI_DRAG_REGION_ATTR = 'data-tauri-drag-region'
  const CLICKABLE_TAGS = new Set([
    'A',
    'BUTTON',
    'INPUT',
    'SELECT',
    'TEXTAREA',
    'LABEL',
    'SUMMARY'
  const INTERACTIVE_ROLES = new Set([
    'button',
    'link',
    'menuitem',
    'tab',
    'checkbox',
    'radio',
    'switch',
    'option'
  function isClickableElement(el) {
    return (
      CLICKABLE_TAGS.has(el.tagName)
      || (el.hasAttribute('contenteditable')
        && el.getAttribute('contenteditable') !== 'false')
      || (el.hasAttribute('tabindex') && el.getAttribute('tabindex') !== '-1')
      || INTERACTIVE_ROLES.has(el.getAttribute('role'))
    )
  // Walk the composed path from target upward.
  // Supported values for data-tauri-drag-region:
  //   (bare / no value / "true") -> self: only direct clicks on this element trigger drag
  //   "deep"                   -> deep: clicks anywhere in the subtree trigger drag
  //   "false"                  -> disabled: drag is blocked here (and for ancestors)
  // Clickable elements (buttons, links, etc.) normally block dragging,
  // but if they themselves carry data-tauri-drag-region they act as drag regions.
  function isDragRegion(composedPath) {
    for (const el of composedPath) {
      if (!(el instanceof HTMLElement)) continue
      const attr = el.getAttribute(TAURI_DRAG_REGION_ATTR)
      // clickable without explicit drag region ??? blocks drag
      if (isClickableElement(el) && attr === null) return false
      // no attr ??? keep walking up
      if (attr === null) continue
      // explicitly disabled
      if (attr === 'false') return false
      // subtree drag ??? any descendant triggers
      if (attr === 'deep') return true
      // bare or "true" attr ??? only direct clicks on this element
      if (attr === '' || attr === 'true') return el === composedPath[0]
    }
    return false
  const osName = __TEMPLATE_os_name__
  // initial mousedown position for macOS
  let initialX = 0
  let initialY = 0
  document.addEventListener('mousedown', (e) => {
    if (
      // was left mouse button
      e.button === 0
      // and was normal click to drag or double click to maximize
      && (e.detail === 1 || e.detail === 2)
      // and is drag region
      && isDragRegion(e.composedPath())
    ) {
      // macOS maximization happens on `mouseup`,
      // so we save needed state and early return
      if (osName === 'macos' && e.detail === 2) {
        initialX = e.clientX
        initialY = e.clientY
        return
      }
      // prevents text cursor
      e.preventDefault()
      // fix #2549: double click on drag region edge causes content to maximize without window sizing change
      // https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/2549#issuecomment-1250036908
      e.stopImmediatePropagation()
      // start dragging if the element has a `tauri-drag-region` data attribute and maximize on double-clicking it
      const cmd = e.detail === 2 ? 'internal_toggle_maximize' : 'start_dragging'
      window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke('plugin:window|' + cmd)
    }
  // on macOS we maximize on mouseup instead, to match the system behavior where maximization can be canceled
  // if the mouse moves outside the data-tauri-drag-region
  if (osName === 'macos') {
    document.addEventListener('mouseup', (e) => {
      if (
        // was left mouse button
        e.button === 0
        // and was double click
        && e.detail === 2
        // and the cursor hasn't moved from initial mousedown
        && e.clientX === initialX
        && e.clientY === initialY
        // and the event path contains a drag region (with no clickable element in between)
        && isDragRegion(e.composedPath())
      ) {
        window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke(
          'plugin:window|internal_toggle_maximize'
        )
      }
    })

// this is a function and not an iife so use it carefully
(function (message) {
  if (
    message instanceof ArrayBuffer
    || ArrayBuffer.isView(message)
    || Array.isArray(message)
  ) {
    return {
      contentType: 'application/octet-stream',
      data: message
    }
  } else {
    const data = JSON.stringify(message, (_k, val) => {
      // if this value changes, make sure to update it in:
      // 1. ipc.js
      // 2. core.ts
      const SERIALIZE_TO_IPC_FN = '__TAURI_TO_IPC_KEY__'
      if (val instanceof Map) {
        return Object.fromEntries(val.entries())
      } else if (val instanceof Uint8Array) {
        return Array.from(val)
      } else if (val instanceof ArrayBuffer) {
        return Array.from(new Uint8Array(val))
      } else if (
        typeof val === 'object'
        && val !== null
        && SERIALIZE_TO_IPC_FN in val
      ) {
        return val[SERIALIZE_TO_IPC_FN]()
      } else {
        return val
      }
    })
    return {
      contentType: 'application/json',
      data
    }

;(function () {
  /**
   * A runtime generated key to ensure an IPC call comes from an initialized frame.
   * This is declared outside the `window.__TAURI_INVOKE__` definition to prevent
   * the key from being leaked by `window.__TAURI_INVOKE__.toString()`.
   */
  const __TAURI_INVOKE_KEY__ = __TEMPLATE_invoke_key__
  const processIpcMessage = __RAW_process_ipc_message_fn__
  const osName = __TEMPLATE_os_name__
  const fetchChannelDataCommand = __TEMPLATE_fetch_channel_data_command__
  let customProtocolIpcFailed = false
  // on Android we never use it because Android does not have support to reading the request body
  const canUseCustomProtocol = osName !== 'android'
  function sendIpcMessage(message) {
    const { cmd, callback, error, payload, options } = message
    if (
      !customProtocolIpcFailed
      && (canUseCustomProtocol || cmd === fetchChannelDataCommand)
    ) {
      const { contentType, data } = processIpcMessage(payload)
      const headers = new Headers((options && options.headers) || {})
      headers.set('Content-Type', contentType)
      headers.set('Tauri-Callback', callback)
      headers.set('Tauri-Error', error)
      headers.set('Tauri-Invoke-Key', __TAURI_INVOKE_KEY__)
      fetch(window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.convertFileSrc(cmd, 'ipc'), {
        method: 'POST',
        body: data,
        headers
      })
        .then((response) => {
          const callbackId =
            response.headers.get('Tauri-Response') === 'ok' ? callback : error
          // we need to split here because on Android the content-type gets duplicated
          switch ((response.headers.get('content-type') || '').split(',')[0]) {
            case 'application/json':
              return response.json().then((r) => [callbackId, r])
            case 'text/plain':
              return response.text().then((r) => [callbackId, r])
            default:
              return response.arrayBuffer().then((r) => [callbackId, r])
          }
        })
        .then(
          ([callbackId, data]) => {
            window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.runCallback(callbackId, data)
          },
          (e) => {
            console.warn(
              'IPC custom protocol failed, Tauri will now use the postMessage interface instead',
              e
            )
            // failed to use the custom protocol IPC (either the webview blocked a custom protocol or it was a CSP error)
            // so we need to fallback to the postMessage interface
            customProtocolIpcFailed = true
            sendIpcMessage(message)
          }
        )
    } else {
      // otherwise use the postMessage interface
      const { data } = processIpcMessage({
        cmd,
        callback,
        error,
        options: {
          ...options,
          customProtocolIpcBlocked: customProtocolIpcFailed
        },
        payload,
        __TAURI_INVOKE_KEY__
      })
      // `window.ipc.postMessage` came from `tauri-runtime-wry` > `wry` [`with_ipc_handler`](https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/blob/a0403b9e2f1ff9d73be7dce1184f058afcaa1d82/src/lib.rs#L1130)
      window.ipc.postMessage(data)
    }
  Object.defineProperty(window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__, 'postMessage', {
    value: sendIpcMessage
